termConflicts.problem: Human-facing prose usually uses 'Rule Set', code identifiers use RuleSet, file paths use rule-sets, and package IDs use rulesets. This is mostly valid but not documented as a terminology policy in one place.
termConflicts.proposedCorrection: Add a glossary normalization note: prose = Rule Set; type/member identifiers = RuleSet; repository folders = rule-sets; package IDs may use rulesets according to manifest/package naming rules.

termConflicts.problem: Several docs discuss publication, while Werewolf demonstrates an intermediate promotion eligibility gate that is not the same as runtime publication.
termConflicts.proposedCorrection: Define lifecycle states for extraction candidate, prototype candidate, approved for promotion, promoted package artifact, and published runtime package.
termConflicts.resolution: Promotion means the package satisfies the declared quality gate for a release scope. Publication means an artifact was distributed through an approved channel. A package may be promotion-eligible or promoted without being published; publication never implies installation, enablement, or activation.

termConflicts.term: complete Rule Set versus current slice
termConflicts.problem: Product docs say MVP needs one complete Rule Set, while the Werewolf baseline demonstrates a current-slice reference with explicit blockers and unsupported capabilities.
termConflicts.proposedCorrection: Clarify whether 'complete Rule Set' means complete MVP-supported slice or complete game-system catalog. This changes acceptance semantics and needs a decision.
termConflicts.resolution: Use declared-scope completeness for release/MVP claims. Source-system completeness means complete source RPG implementation and is not required for MVP.

termConflicts.term: documentation prototype / package source / packaged artifact / installed artifact
termConflicts.problem: Before DR-0004, the docs did not normatively distinguish review evidence, source inputs, build output, and local installation.
termConflicts.proposedCorrection: Define materialization-role terminology and authority boundaries.
termConflicts.resolution: SPEC-0001 and RFC-0027 now distinguish documentation prototype, package source, packaged artifact, and installed artifact. Filesystem presence alone confers no executable, packaging, installation, activation, Campaign-binding, promotion, or publication authority.
